Outboard 100-hour and 300-hour service at your dock

Scheduled service is the cheapest thing you will ever do to an outboard. We send a mechanic who knows your engine to your lift, slip, or driveway, with the right oil, filters, plugs, and impeller for your make and model.

What's included

  • Engine oil and filter
  • Gear lube (lower unit) with a check for water intrusion
  • Spark plugs
  • Fuel filter and fuel-water separator
  • Water pump impeller at 300 hours or 3 years, or sooner if the stream is weak
  • Thermostat and poppet check
  • Grease fittings, trim and tilt, steering
  • Anodes, prop, and corrosion check
  • Battery and charging test
  • Engine computer scan for stored fault codes
When

Every 100 hours or once a year, whichever comes first. In salt water, once a year even if you barely used it. The 300-hour service adds the water pump, thermostats, and a deeper fuel-system check.

Time on site

2 to 4 hours for one engine

What it usually costs here

$350 to $900 per engine for a 100-hour; $900 to $2,000 for a full 300-hour with impeller and thermostats. Mechanics set their own rates.

In Tampa Bay specifically

Tampa Bay boats run year-round, so the 'annual' service is really a sun and salt service. Ethanol fuel plus summer heat is the number one cause of the fuel problems mechanics find during these visits.

Engines

YamahaMercurySuzukiHonda MarineTohatsu

Questions we get

Do I need to be there?

No. Most customers leave the keys in a lockbox or the boat on the lift. The mechanic texts photos of what was done and the old parts.

Can you service a boat on a lift?

Yes. Lift-kept boats are most of what we do. The mechanic brings ear muffs or a bucket to run the engine, or lowers the boat if the lift allows.

What if the mechanic finds something else?

You get a call and a written quote before any extra work. Nothing is added to the bill without your OK.

Do you use OEM parts?

Mechanics default to the manufacturer's service kit. If a non-OEM part is used, it is listed on the invoice.
